messages:
incident-bot: PAGE: P1 - serving-runtime cluster (us-east-1) - multiple pods OOM/crash + pod evictions due to ephemeral-storage pressure. Pager: oncall-ops.

alex: ack, I'm on it. seeing alerts for ~8 pods in namespace=redwood-serving in CrashLoopBackOff / Evicted.

mira: saw the same, tracer shows increased 5xxs and latency to the hosted API. customers affected: some realtime chat sessions.

alex: quick dump from one affected node:
```
$ kubectl describe pod redwood-runtime-7f8b9 -n redwood-serving
Status: Failed
Reason: Evicted
Message: The node was low on resource: ephemeral-storage. Container runtime tried to reclaim space.
```

alex: and df -h on node (ssh):
```
/var/lib/model-cache 100G 100G 0 100% /var/lib/model-cache
/var/log              50G 49G  1G 98% /var/log
```

jonah: yikes. NVM, this is the model cache dir filling and also log sprawl. nvidia-smi shows no GPU OOMs, this is disk eviction causing container exits which then produce more logs (chicken-egg).

pete: can we confirm kubelet eviction log?

alex: tail of /var/log/kubelet.log shows:
```
E eviction manager: pods for eviction: 8, reason: nodefs.available < 10%
I eviction manager: evicting pod redwood-runtime-7f8b9 due to ephemeral-storage
```

anya: any automated fallback in place? do requests retry to alternative region or degrade gracefully?

mira: currently small fallback to smaller model exists but routing is sticky for some routes. traffic blip visible for a subset of customers. I opened an incident page.

alex: live mitigation plan (short-term):
- identify top files in /var/lib/model-cache and /var/log.
- remove stale model shards and compress old logs.
- evict a few non-critical pods to let kubelet free space (kubectl delete pod ...) so critical runtime can restart.
- cordon the node and move traffic away: `kubectl cordon ip-10-0-7-23` and drain low-priority pods.

jonah: I'm running a quick du: `du -sh /var/lib/model-cache/* | sort -h | tail -n 20` to find biggest models.

jonah: largest offenders: 
- 65G: /var/lib/model-cache/vllm-xlarge-2025
- 18G: /var/lib/model-cache/gptq-13b-quant
- 7G: /var/lib/model-cache/old/

pete: if we rm a model shard we will drop cache warmness; ok for short term. suggest removing `vllm-xlarge-2025` copy on this node (it's replicated elsewhere).

alex: executing safe cleanup: `rm -rf /var/lib/model-cache/vllm-xlarge-2025/*` (only on node ip-10-0-7-23) - will coordinate so not all replicas removed at once.

alex: also rotating logs: `gzip -9 /var/log/redwood/*.log && rm -f /var/log/redwood/*.log.1` - freeing ~30G.

oncall-ops: please confirm you want us to proceed with deletions; I can take over if you want to remain on-call.

mira: proceed, do one node at a time and confirm downstream health checks pass. set a 5-minute observation window after restart.

alex: doing node1 cleanup now.

incident-bot: note: automated alerting suppressed for 10m for this node while we remediate.

alex: post-cleanup df -h: /var/lib/model-cache now 42G used of 100G (freed ~58G). /var/log down to 35G.

alex: restarted runtime container on node; pod came back UP in 42s, readiness OK.

mira: metrics: error rate falling from 6.2% -> 0.9% for the last 10m. latency back to normal. customer-facing errors present during window: ~1200 failed requests total, concentrated in a small set of API keys.

anya: should we open a customer notice? Product recommended we proactively reach out to top-affected customers.

pete: yes, ops to draft. severity: P1 -> mitigation done for node1, but other nodes show similar pressure.

alex: repeating cleanup in parallel on node2 and node3 with staggered 10m to avoid correlated restarts.

jonah: investigating root cause: model cache retention policy didn't evict older replicas when disk pressure grew due to a recent spike in model downloads (continuous eval run + a canary model rollout). We also found logrotate misconfiguration: `logrotate` for /var/log/redwood had maxsize=200M but was not running due to a missing symlink.

mira: good find. next steps for medium-term (postmortem):
- fix model-cache GC to respect node disk pressure and prefer removing least-recently-used replicas.
- convert model-cache from ephemeral storage -> PVC backed on heavy nodes.
- fix logrotate symlink and cap total log retention to 10G per node.
- add alert that correlates model-download spikes + disk-usage.

oncall-ops: Alex, handoff to Ops for remediation runbook and customer comms. I'm taking the oncall.

alex: handoff acked. leaving notes: nodes cleaned: ip-10-0-7-23, ip-10-0-8-45. nodes remaining under watch: ip-10-0-9-12 (cleaning queued).

mira: customer impact summary for postmortem:
- duration: ~00:28 - 01:20 UTC window for peak impact (approx 52 minutes)
- affected region: us-east-1 (hosted inference)
- approx requests failed: 1,200 failed, 15k degraded (higher latency)
- visible customer reports: 3 → ticketed and triaged by support.

anya: assigning post-incident owners:
- root cause + infra change: jonah + eng-runtime
- logrotate & runbooks: pete + eng-sre
- customer comms + support sync: mira + customer-success

alex: final note: we should add a kill-switch to reduce model download rate from model-catalog during heavy periods to avoid repo stampedes.

oncall-ops: confirmed mitigation complete; monitoring for 3 hours. creating follow-up incident retrospective.

incident-bot: Incident closed to P2 for monitoring; create postmortem ticket: PM-1865432100 in internal tracker.

mira: thanks all, good coordination. :thumbsup:

alex: I'll update the runbook with cleanup commands and safe deletion checklist.

pete: leaving a comment to limit node-local cache size to 50G as a short-term config until PVC transition done.

anya: adding retrospective action: test canary model rollout in staging with model-download throttling.

-- end of thread --
